items.title: Meta Andromeda: Powering the Next Generation of Ads Retrieval Through Model-System Co-Design
items.abstract: This post describes the next generation of Meta Andromeda, Meta’s personalized ads retrieval engine, and how co-designing the model, system, and GPU hardware unlocks a new efficiency frontier for ads retrieval. In production, the system scores every eligible ad with near ranking-level model performance at retrieval scale and surfaces the top candidates at over one billion ads per second, a new throughput benchmark for ads retrieval-stage models (i.e., a 100x lift compared to the 2024 Meta Andromeda system). For advertisers, this means better performance automatically from the retrieval system matching ads across a larger candidate pool, within the same latency budget. Since 2025, Meta Andromeda has delivered a 2.4% increase in conversions on Facebook. Meta Andromeda is Meta’s machine learning system for personalized ads retrieval, the first stage of the ads recommendation pipeline. Retrieval narrows a vast pool of eligible ads down to a small set of strong candidates in milliseconds; a later, more computationally expensive ranking stage then scores those survivors in fine detail. Historically, the deep modeling quality of the ranking stage has been too costly to apply at retrieval’s scale. Building on the retrieval foundation established with Andromeda’s 2024 launch on the NVIDIA GH200 Grace Hopper Superchip, this post shares how co-designing the model, system, and hardware together brings near ranking-level performance to the retrieval scale. Challenges and Opportunities in Scaling Retrieval The 2024 Andromeda deployment reimplemented retrieval with an end-to-end optimized retrieval implementation from custom AI hardware with hierarchical indexing and GPU-native operators to a purpose-built ML model, growing model capacity by four orders of magnitude. Since then, generative AI creative tools have helped advertisers rapidly create hundreds of millions of new ads, growing Meta’s ads candidate pool to an unprecedented scale. Scoring such a large ad candidate pool with a more accurate model at a much higher system throughput requires fundamental technology breakthroughs in model quality, system architecture, and hardware utilization jointly. Higher Model Performance Requires a New Architecture Ads retrieval has an outsized ROI on incremental quality: Small improvements in retrieval model performance can drive large gains in advertiser value. The rapid expansion of our ads candidate pool makes optimizing for hardware capacity ROI an increasingly critical factor. The 2024 Meta Andromeda retrieval models have established a highly effective foundation with their GPU-optimized deep neural network architecture. To keep improving retrieval performance at a sustainable compute cost at our current scale, however, we must move beyond that paradigm. This requires a fundamental architectural evolution to push model performance boundaries significantly without a proportional increase in costs. New System Bottlenecks at Billion Scale The 2024 Meta Andromeda system evaluates at tens of millions of ads per second per GPU card. Meeting the new business demand requires a throughput at multi-billion ads evaluated per second per card in the system. At billions of ads per second throughput, the memory bandwidth of passing ad tensors through memory hierarchy becomes the new bottleneck. Intermediate tensors between GPU kernels account for terabytes per second of memory traffic, and shipping ads between local CPU hosts and remote hardware accelerators evaluating models saturates the network link. This requires a new system co-design that unifies these fragmented, distributed workloads into a single GPU pipeline. Pushing Towards the Hardware Limits With retrieval running on GPU, the important optimization question is “How close are we to the hardware ceiling, and how much room remains for future model growth?” Answering this requires pushing each component of the retrieval pipeline to the limits of the current hardware generation, a challenge that motiva

items.summary: Meta가 광고 추천 파이프라인의 첫 단계인 Andromeda 검색 엔진의 차세대 버전을 공개했다. 모델, 시스템, GPU 하드웨어를 함께 설계해 랭킹 단계에 근접한 모델 품질을 검색 규모에서 구현했으며, 초당 **10억 건 이상의 광고**를 평가해 2024년 Andromeda 대비 **100배** 처리량을 달성했다. 생성형 AI 창작 도구로 광고 후보 풀이 급격히 커지면서 기존 GPU 최적화 심층신경망 구조만으로는 비용 효율적 성능 개선이 어려워져, 아키텍처 전환과 함께 GPU 커널 간 텐서 전송, CPU-가속기 간 네트워크 병목 등을 해소하는 단일 GPU 파이프라인으로 시스템을 재설계했다. 이 결과 2025년 이후 Facebook에서 전환율이 2.4% 증가했다.
items.why_it_matters: 검색 단계에서 랭킹 수준의 모델 정확도를 확보하면 광고주 가치에 큰 영향을 미치는 동시에, 급증하는 생성형 AI 기반 광고 후보 풀을 처리하기 위한 하드웨어·시스템 공동설계 사례로서 대규모 추천 시스템 설계에 참고할 만하다.
items.whats_different: 2024년 NVIDIA GH200 기반 Andromeda 시스템이 카드당 초당 수천만 건 처리에 그쳤던 것과 달리, 이번 버전은 모델·시스템·하드웨어를 함께 재설계해 **초당 10억 건 이상**으로 처리량을 끌어올렸다.

items.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
items.abstract: If you’ve tried to get an agent into production, the model and tool use are not the blocker. The main bottleneck is everything around them: how many teams can build within a secure environment, which team owns each model and tool, how AgentOps and error handling stay inside a pre-defined boundary, and how platform, Workstream, and finance teams see cost and health across accounts. For a Platform team that wants to support many agentic use cases, that’s a platform product to design and operate. In this post, we refer to the team that manages the platform as the Platform team, and to the teams that build on it as Workstream teams. Workstream teams are the domain or product teams that build and own agents on the platform. Each Workstream team needs a paved road with approved models and tools, short-lived workload identity, isolated runtime and memory, automated evaluation, rollback, telemetry, and cost attribution. These controls need to remain consistent as Workstream teams customize prompts, tools, data access, and application behavior. When every team assembles them, controls drift, shared services become a bottleneck, and ownership is difficult to audit. In this post, we walk through the architecture and reference implementation of an enterprise Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover the multi-account operating model, the Platform control plane, a repeatable per-Workstream deployment pattern, separate inference and tool gateways, and an evaluation pipeline that gates each agent before promotion to production. By the end, you should be able to deploy a governed Workstream from the companion blueprint, validate its security and lifecycle contracts, and use it as the foundation for your own agentic AI platform in the organization. Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides modular services for building, deploying, and operating agents at scale, including runtime, gateway, identity, memory, policy, registry, and evaluations. The Enterprise Agentic AI Platform Blueprint , built on AgentCore, adds the surrounding enterprise contracts as deployable infrastructure as code: ownership, account boundaries, software delivery, observability, cost governance, and retirement. Architectural principles Before diving into the solution details, it helps to understand the organizational needs that drive the platform architecture. The common challenges we have heard from customers who establish an agent platform fall into these five categories: Governed model access: Every untrusted inference request must pass through an approved inference gateway. The gateway applies the organization’s guardrails (for example, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails or a third-party provider), restricts which models and inference AWS Regions each Workstream can use, and enforces per-Workstream rate limits, token quotas, and budgets so that no single team can exhaust shared capacity. It also carries workload identity and emits attribution data. Governed tool access: Agents must discover and invoke only approved tools through an authenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway, with exact targets, least-privilege execution roles, policy decisions, and an auditable owner. Delegated delivery: Workstream teams (for example, product teams) need to ship and roll back independently inside pre-approved boundaries, without waiting for the platform team to deploy each application or granting developers a direct infrastructure write path. Fleet operations and cost: Several personas need visibility across accounts without gaining write access to team workloads. Agent operations engineers need logs, metrics, traces, and quotas. Workstream owners need cost per agent against their budgets. FinOps and finance teams need chargeback by team or business unit through AWS Cost Explorer and the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR) . items.title_ko: AWS, Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 기반 엔터프라이즈 Agentic AI 플랫폼 블루프린트 공개
items.summary: AWS는 에이전트 프로덕션 배포의 진짜 병목이 모델·도구 자체가 아니라 거버넌스, 소유권, 비용 추적 같은 주변 체계라고 지적한다. 이를 해결하기 위해 Amazon Bedrock과 **Amazon Bedrock AgentCore**(런타임, 게이트웨이, 아이덴티티, 메모리, 정책, 레지스트리, 평가 기능 포함) 위에 멀티 계정 운영 모델, 플랫폼 제어 플레인, 워크스트림별 반복 가능한 배포 패턴을 구현한 참조 아키텍처를 제시한다. 추론용·도구용 게이트웨이를 분리하고, 프로덕션 승격 전 각 에이전트를 검증하는 평가 파이프라인을 포함한다. 이 블루프린트는 소유권, 계정 경계, 소프트웨어 배포, 관측성, 비용 거버넌스, 폐기 절차를 코드형 인프라로 제공한다.
items.why_it_matters: 여러 팀이 동시에 에이전트를 구축하는 조직에서는 각 팀이 통제 체계를 개별적으로 만들 경우 **거버넌스가 흐트러지고** 공유 서비스가 병목이 되며 책임 소재 감사가 어려워지는데, 이는 많은 기업이 겪는 공통 문제다.
items.whats_different: 기존에는 플랫폼팀이 각 워크스트림 애플리케이션 배포를 직접 처리하거나 개발자에게 인프라 쓰기 권한을 부여해야 했던 반면, 이 블루프린트는 사전 승인된 경계 내에서 워크스트림팀이 독립적으로 배포·롤백할 수 있는 위임형 전달 구조를 제공한다.

items.title: Timestral
items.abstract: We introduce Timestral, a family of four time series foundation models for probabilistic forecasting, with 5M, 28M, 123M, and 209M parameters. Timestral sets a new state of the art on GIFT-Eval, TIME, and fev-bench, where Timestral-209M and Timestral-123M take the top two places on every metric. We achieve this with three ingredients: Decoupled Horizon Forecasting (DHF), which separates prediction tokens from the causally encoded context, so that longer horizons are trained without masking context and each observed value is both a forecast target and context for later forecasts; a covariate framework that natively supports known-future covariates within a causal architecture; and a two-stage pipeline that pretrains exclusively on a diverse, large-scale synthetic corpus before post-training on a mix of real and synthetic data with extended context. This report describes the model design and its benchmark results. Weights for all four models are available on Hugging Face and inference code on GitHub.
items.title_ko: Timestral 공개 — 5M~209M 시계열 예측 모델 4종, GIFT-Eval·TIME·fev-bench 전 지표 1위
items.summary: Timestral은 확률적 시계열 예측을 위한 5M, 28M, 123M, 209M 파라미터 규모의 파운데이션 모델 4종이다. GIFT-Eval, TIME, fev-bench 벤치마크에서 새로운 state of the art를 달성했으며, 특히 **Timestral-209M과 123M이 모든 지표에서 1, 2위**를 차지했다. 핵심 기법은 예측 토큰과 인과 인코딩된 컨텍스트를 분리해 긴 horizon도 마스킹 없이 학습 가능한 Decoupled Horizon Forecasting(DHF), 인과적 구조 안에서 미래 공변량을 자연스럽게 다루는 covariate 프레임워크, 그리고 대규모 합성 데이터로 사전학습 후 실제·합성 혼합 데이터와 확장된 컨텍스트로 후처리하는 2단계 파이프라인이다. 모델 가중치는 Hugging Face에, 추론 코드는 GitHub에 공개되었다.
items.why_it_matters: 소규모(5M)부터 중형(209M)까지 다양한 크기의 시계열 파운데이션 모델을 공개함으로써 자원 제약 환경부터 고성능 요구 환경까지 폭넓게 적용 가능한 예측 모델 선택지를 제공한다.
items.whats_different: DHF 구조로 예측 토큰과 컨텍스트를 분리해 긴 horizon 학습 시 마스킹이 필요했던 **기존 인과적 시계열 모델 대비** 관측값을 예측 타깃이자 컨텍스트로 동시에 활용할 수 있다.

items.title: Distributed training with Ray Train DLCs and EFA on EKS
items.abstract: What usually stops PyTorch training from scaling out to a cluster is the container, not the model code. Every container needs the same CUDA runtime , a PyTorch build compiled against it, NCCL (NVIDIA Collective Communications Library), the Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) userspace libraries, the AWS OFI NCCL plugin that connects NCCL to EFA, and a Ray version the cluster operator agrees with. Building that image and rebuilding it each time one of those pieces moves is a project of its own, and it has nothing to do with the model you set out to train. The Ray Train Deep Learning Container (DLC) is that image, built by AWS. AWS assembles the stack, tests it as one unit, publishes it in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) Public and keeps it patched. Figure 1: One EKS cluster with a control plane managed by AWS, a CPU system node (m7i.xlarge) running the KubeRay operator and Ray head, and two EFA-enabled g6.12xlarge nodes in one Availability Zone. KubeRay builds it from one RayCluster manifest, Ray Train places eight workers, one per GPU, and inter-node collectives cross over EFA. Ray runs a job across machines as a single cluster with two roles. The Ray head coordinates and runs the global control store that tracks cluster state, the dashboard and job server you submit jobs to. Ray worker nodes supply the GPUs and run the training processes. Each worker joins the cluster by connecting to the head’s address when it starts. On Kubernetes, each of these is a pod. Kubernetes has no built-in idea of a Ray cluster, so something must create the head and worker pods, start Ray in the right role in each, point the workers at the head, and replace pods that fail. KubeRay does this. It’s an open source Kubernetes operator that adds a RayCluster resource: you describe a head group and a worker group in one manifest, and KubeRay builds and maintains the cluster from it. A single tagged image runs as both the Ray head and the Ray workers, whether KubeRay starts it on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) or you start it yourself on Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2). What you add is configuration: which instances, how many GPUs each pod gets, which network transport NCCL uses, and which extra Python packages a job needs. All of it is set from outside the image. This post walks through a sample that uses the DLC exactly as published to fine-tune Qwen2.5-1.5B with PyTorch Fully Sharded Data Parallel (FSDP) across eight NVIDIA L4 GPUs on two g6.12xlarge instances. The training code is one function, the cluster is one RayCluster manifest plus a file of variables, and no image is built at any point. Because the DLC already carries the EFA stack, collectives between the two instances run over the EFA as soon as the pods request it. The entire solution is in this sample repository , and it uses the same KubeRay-on-EKS foundation as our multi-node Ray Serve walkthrough . What you get without building anything The Ray Train DLC is the PyTorch training image with Ray’s training libraries on top. items.title_ko: AWS, EKS·EFA 기반 Ray Train DLC 공개 — 이미지 빌드 없이 Qwen2.5-1.5B 8-GPU 분산학습
items.summary: AWS가 PyTorch, CUDA, NCCL, EFA 유저스페이스 라이브러리, AWS OFI NCCL 플러그인, Ray를 하나로 묶어 테스트·패치한 Ray Train Deep Learning Container(DLC)를 ECR Public에 공개했다. KubeRay가 RayCluster 매니페스트 하나로 헤드와 워커 파드를 구성하며, 동일한 이미지가 Ray 헤드와 워커 양쪽에서 실행된다. 이 글은 g6.12xlarge 2대, L4 GPU 8개 환경에서 해당 DLC를 그대로 써서 **Qwen2.5-1.5B를 PyTorch FSDP로 파인튜닝**하는 예제를 다룬다. 학습 코드는 함수 하나, 클러스터 설정은 RayCluster 매니페스트와 변수 파일 하나로 구성되며 이미지 빌드 과정이 전혀 없다. DLC에 EFA 스택이 이미 포함돼 있어 파드가 요청하는 즉시 두 인스턴스 간 collective 통신이 EFA를 통해 이루어진다.
items.why_it_matters: 분산 학습 확장을 가로막는 주된 요인이 모델 코드가 아니라 CUDA·NCCL·EFA 버전을 맞춘 컨테이너 빌드·유지보수라는 점을 짚어, MLOps 담당자가 반복적으로 겪는 인프라 부담을 줄여준다는 점에서 의미가 있다.
items.whats_different: 기존에는 CUDA, PyTorch, NCCL, EFA 설치 프로그램, AWS OFI NCCL 플러그인, Ray 버전을 팀이 직접 맞춰 빌드·갱신해야 했던 것과 달리, **Ray Train DLC**는 AWS가 이 스택 전체를 하나의 이미지로 조립·검증·배포해 별도 빌드 없이 그대로 사용할 수 있다.

items.title: V-LUMEN: Visual Lookup Memory for Embedding Scaling in Vision-Language Models
items.abstract: Embedding-level scaling expands the capacity of language models through lookup-based memory rather than by increasing model depth, width, or dense computation. Extending this idea to vision-language models (VLMs) is challenging because visual features are continuous, spatially structured, and query-dependent, unlike discrete text tokens that naturally support n-gram lookup. We introduce V-LUMEN, a visual lookup memory for VLMs. V-LUMEN discretizes visual features with a frozen codebook, builds spatially aware memory keys through spatial aggregation-based hashing, and modulates them with text-conditioned relevance signals; all addressing is non-parametric, and the retrieved embeddings are fused into the backbone through a gated residual pathway. On five reasoning-intensive benchmarks, V-LUMEN substantially improves a frozen Qwen3-VL-2B backbone and transfers zero-shot to three benchmarks whose images are disjoint from the training data. At a matched parameter budget, moving part of a LoRA or MoE adapter's capacity into V-LUMEN preserves accuracy on two backbones, indicating that external visual memory is an independent capacity axis rather than a stronger adaptation method. Because lookup cost is constant in table size and incurred only once at prefill, this capacity grows in storage rather than in per-token compute. Code is available at https://github.com/miso-choi/V-Lumen.
items.title_ko: V-LUMEN, 비전-언어모델에 시각 조회 메모리 도입 — Qwen3-VL-2B 고정 백본 성능 대폭 개선, 제로샷 전이도 확인
items.summary: V-LUMEN은 언어모델의 임베딩 수준 스케일링 아이디어를 시각-언어모델(VLM)로 확장한 조회 기반 메모리 기법이다. 고정된 코드북으로 시각 특징을 이산화하고, 공간 집계 기반 해싱으로 공간 인식 메모리 키를 구성하며, 텍스트 조건 관련성 신호로 이를 변조한다. 모든 주소 지정은 비매개변수적이며, 검색된 임베딩은 게이트형 잔차 경로를 통해 백본에 융합된다. **5개의 추론 집약적 벤치마크**에서 고정된 Qwen3-VL-2B 백본의 성능을 크게 향상시켰고, 학습 데이터와 겹치지 않는 이미지로 구성된 3개 벤치마크에 제로샷으로 전이되었다. 동일 파라미터 예산에서 LoRA나 MoE 어댑터 용량 일부를 V-LUMEN으로 옮겨도 정확도가 유지되어, 외부 시각 메모리가 독립적인 용량 축임을 보여준다.
items.why_it_matters: 조회 비용이 테이블 크기와 무관하게 일정하고 prefill 시 한 번만 발생하므로, 모델 용량을 **저장 공간**으로 확장하면서 토큰당 연산량 증가 없이 성능을 끌어올릴 수 있는 새로운 스케일링 축을 제시한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 LoRA나 MoE 같은 어댑터 기반 용량 확장 방식과 달리, V-LUMEN은 비매개변수적 조회 메모리를 통해 **독립적인 용량 축**을 제공하며 동일 파라미터 예산에서도 어댑터 용량 일부를 대체해도 정확도를 유지함을 보인다.

items.title: Pneuma: A Large-Scale Real-World Time Series Benchmark for Commercial Aircraft Predictive Maintenance
items.abstract: Predictive maintenance is vital for commercial aviation, yet progress remains hindered by the lack of public, large-scale real-world datasets. As a result, most methods are developed and evaluated on proprietary data, limiting reproducibility. We introduce Pneuma, the first publicly available large-scale benchmark for predictive maintenance using onboard time series from in-service commercial aircraft. Built around bleed air systems, Pneuma contains over 920 million multivariate time steps across four aircraft types and 9 verified fault scenarios, directly aligned with real maintenance logs. The dataset exhibits key real-world challenges, including substantial class imbalance, subtle fault evolution patterns, and significant variance across aircraft configurations. We structure the benchmark around three tasks: multivariate forecasting, supervised fault classification, and unsupervised anomaly detection, with labels derived from actual maintenance records. Under unified settings, we evaluate over 25 models from four methodological families on 9 carefully curated subsets. The results reveal that even strong contemporary models struggle with subtle fault signatures. Further analyses show consistent gains from additional in-context examples and multivariate inference, while forecasting quality is strongly associated with anomaly detection performance. Together, these findings provide practical insights into effectively modeling complex real-world aviation time series. We hope Pneuma will serve as a rigorous and reproducible foundation for advancing data-driven predictive maintenance toward real-world deployment in commercial aviation.
items.title_ko: Pneuma 공개 — 상업 항공기 9억2천만 시점 실제 시계열로 예측정비 벤치마크 구축, 25개 모델 평가
items.summary: Pneuma는 실제 운항 중인 상업 항공기의 블리드 에어 시스템 데이터를 기반으로 한 최초의 공개 대규모 예측정비 벤치마크다. 4개 기종, 9개 검증된 고장 시나리오에 걸쳐 **9억2천만 개 이상의 다변량 시계열**을 포함하며, 실제 정비 기록과 직접 연계된 레이블을 제공한다. 데이터셋은 심각한 클래스 불균형, 미묘한 고장 진행 패턴, 기종 간 큰 변동성 등 현실적인 난제를 그대로 담고 있다. 다변량 예측, 지도 기반 고장 분류, 비지도 이상 탐지 세 가지 과제로 구성되며, 4개 방법론 계열의 25개 이상 모델을 9개 세분화된 서브셋에서 평가한 결과 최신 모델들도 미묘한 고장 신호 포착에 어려움을 겪는 것으로 나타났다. 추가로 인컨텍스트 예시 활용과 다변량 추론이 성능 향상에 기여하며, 예측 품질이 이상 탐지 성능과 강하게 연관됨을 확인했다.
items.why_it_matters: 그동안 예측정비 연구는 비공개 데이터에 의존해 재현성이 떨어졌는데, Pneuma는 실제 항공 운항 데이터를 공개함으로써 **재현 가능한 비교 기준**을 제공해 데이터 기반 항공 정비 연구의 실질적 진전을 가능하게 한다.
items.whats_different: 기존 연구들이 소규모 비공개 또는 시뮬레이션 데이터에 의존했던 것과 달리, Pneuma는 실제 정비 기록과 연계된 대규모 공개 데이터셋으로 클래스 불균형과 기종 간 변동성 같은 현실적 난제를 그대로 보존했다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
items.abstract: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

items.title: Identifying and disentangling direct and spillover effects using multiple pre-treatment periods
items.abstract: Under interference, the treatment of some units affects the outcomes of others, so that the effect on a treated unit consists of a direct and a spillover component. A non-treated comparison group then generally identifies neither component, but the difference between the total effect on the treated and the spillover effect on the comparison units. We show that both components are identified separately when multiple pre-treatment periods are available, without an uncontaminated comparison group. Under no anticipation, pre-treatment outcomes are free of both components for every unit. Extrapolating the pre-treatment trend within a group, as in interrupted time series approaches, therefore identifies the counterfactual outcome in the absence of any treatment. Applied to the treated it gives the total effect on them, applied to the non-treated at a given level of exposure the spillover effect on them. Disentangling the two components in addition requires effect homogeneity across treated and non-treated units with the same exposure and covariates, as well as common support in exposure. We derive doubly robust and Neyman-orthogonal expressions for the effects of interest, which permits controlling for covariates by machine learning, and establish asymptotic normality. A simulation study confirms the root-$n$ behaviour of the estimators and the reliability of the standard errors. We apply the framework to the compulsory licensing of enemy-owned patents in the United States in 1919. Licensing raised patenting in the licensed subclasses and in technologically close ones alike, so that a comparison-group design understates the total effect.
items.title_ko: 처치 전 다중 시점 활용해 직접효과와 파급효과 분리 식별 — 1919년 특허 강제실시 사례로 검증
items.summary: 간섭(interference) 상황에서는 처치받은 단위의 효과가 직접효과와 파급효과로 구성되는데, 비처치 비교집단만으로는 이 두 효과를 분리할 수 없고 총효과와 파급효과의 차이만 식별된다. 이 논문은 처치 전 다중 시점 자료가 있으면 오염되지 않은 비교집단 없이도 두 효과를 각각 식별할 수 있음을 보인다. 예상 없음(no anticipation) 가정 하에, 집단 내 처치 전 추세를 외삽하면 무처치 반사실 결과를 구할 수 있고, 이를 처치군과 노출 수준별 비처치군에 각각 적용해 총효과와 파급효과를 구한다. 두 효과를 완전히 분리하려면 동일 노출·공변량을 가진 처치군과 비처치군 간 효과 동질성과 노출의 공통지지(common support) 조건이 추가로 필요하며, 머신러닝으로 공변량을 통제할 수 있는 **이중강건(doubly robust)** 추정량을 유도하고 점근정규성을 증명했다. 1919년 미국의 적국 소유 특허 강제실시 사례에 적용한 결과, 실시된 하위분류뿐 아니라 기술적으로 인접한 분류에서도 특허출원이 증가해 비교집단 설계는 **총효과를 과소추정**함을 보였다.
items.why_it_matters: 네트워크 효과, 정책 파급, 경쟁사 반응 등 간섭이 존재하는 환경에서 비교집단 기반 DID 설계가 체계적으로 효과를 과소/과대평가할 수 있음을 보여주며, 파급효과를 무시한 정책 평가의 위험성을 시사한다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 비처치 비교집단에 의존하는 DID 설계가 총효과와 파급효과를 혼동해 총효과를 과소추정하는 것과 달리, 이 방법은 추가적인 비교집단 없이 처치 전 다중 시점의 추세 외삽만으로 두 효과를 분리 식별한다.

items.title: When uncertainty quantification fails: structural vulnerabilities and corrections for selective prediction under clinical class imbalance
items.abstract: Background. Selective prediction systems improve the safety of clinical artificial intelligence by deferring ambiguous cases to human experts while automating high-confidence decisions. However, this safety mechanism relies entirely on the premise that uncertainty scores accurately reflect clinical ambiguity. In prognostic tasks characterized by severe class imbalance, where the clinical outcome of interest is a minority, this assumption breaks down. Standard uncertainty measures cease to capture clinically aligned ambiguity; instead, they become a proxy for class membership, systematically penalizing minority patients regardless of their individual predictive clarity. Results. Across 56 synthetic conditions and three neurodegenerative cohorts spanning severe class imbalance to near-balanced conditions (multiple sclerosis, Parkinson's Disease, Alzheimer's Disease), our framework consistently maintained bounded, balanced risk across trajectories. In contrast, global metrics either collapsed minority Sensitivity or protected the minority at the expense of majority patients. Applying CCR with standard entropy fails to protect the minority because it breaks within-class monotonicity when tau=0.5. Combining CCR with threshold-aware metrics restores strict monotonicity, correctly identifies ambiguous patients, and safely mitigates minority exclusion. Conclusions. Under clinical class imbalance, standard uncertainty quantification measures dataset sparsity rather than clinical ambiguity, creating a systemic illusion of safety. This bias is a correctable structural flaw. Clinical pipelines deploying selective prediction under imbalance should adopt threshold-aligned uncertainty measures and class-stratified evaluation. This reduces class-specific risk imbalance, supporting safer selective prediction under the evaluated conditions without silently excluding the most vulnerable patients.
items.title_ko: 임상 클래스 불균형 하에서 불확실성 정량화의 구조적 결함 — CCR과 임계값 인지 지표로 소수군 배제 해소
items.summary: 선택적 예측 시스템은 불확실한 사례를 사람에게 넘기고 확실한 경우만 자동화하는 방식으로 임상 AI 안전성을 높이지만, 이는 불확실성 점수가 실제 임상적 모호성을 정확히 반영한다는 전제에 의존한다. 그러나 소수 클래스인 예후가 심한 불균형을 보이는 과제에서는 표준 불확실성 지표가 모호성이 아니라 클래스 소속 여부의 대리 지표로 변질되어, 개별 환자의 예측 명확성과 무관하게 소수군 환자를 체계적으로 불리하게 만든다. 56개 합성 조건과 다발성 경화증·파킨슨병·알츠하이머병 세 신경퇴행성 질환 코호트에 걸친 실험에서, 저자들의 프레임워크는 **불균형이 심한 조건부터 거의 균형잡힌 조건까지 일관되게 균형 잡힌 위험**을 유지한 반면, 전역 지표들은 소수군 민감도를 붕괴시키거나 다수군을 희생시켜 소수군을 보호했다. 표준 엔트로피 기반 CCR은 tau=0.5에서 클래스 내 단조성이 깨져 소수군 보호에 실패하지만, CCR을 임계값 인지 지표와 결합하면 단조성이 회복되어 모호한 환자를 올바르게 식별하고 소수군 배제를 안전하게 완화한다.
items.why_it_matters: 선택적 예측은 임상 AI 안전 장치로 각광받지만, 이 연구는 그 안전성이 **클래스 불균형 하에서는 허상일 수 있음**을 보여줘 배포 중인 임상 파이프라인의 신뢰성 검증이 시급함을 시사한다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 표준 불확실성 측정(엔트로피 기반)과 전역 평가 지표 대비, 임계값 정렬 불확실성 측정과 클래스 계층화 평가를 결합한 접근이 단조성을 유지하면서 소수군 배제 없이 균형 잡힌 위험을 달성한다는 점이 다르다.

items.title: Meta Models: Models that Model Learning
items.abstract: Every neural-network training run produces not only a model, but also evidence about how models learn. Can these accumulated experiments enable us to predict and compare new training runs before executing them? We study meta-models: models that predict the learning behavior of other models. From this perspective, final-performance prediction, learning-curve prediction, and hyperparameter selection are different queries to the same training response function. We take a first, humble empirical step toward this goal: treating real language-model training records as native numeric data, we find that an off-the-shelf tabular in-context learner, TabPFN, can match or outperform a fine-tuned LLM meta-model in multiple evaluated settings. Whereas recent work fine-tunes LLMs on tokenized configurations at a cost of tens to hundreds of GPU-hours, TabPFN requires seconds of fit-and-predict time without task-specific weight updates. We argue that meta-modeling is better treated as its own numeric modality rather than as a text task for LLMs. Going one step further, augmenting TabPFN with Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) further improves accuracy on selected prediction tasks. Finally, we pre-registered a forecast of the Marin Hero Run, a 535B-parameter public training run, whose ground truth is revealed point by point as training progresses, putting meta-model predictions to the test against training outcomes not yet observed at the time of forecasting.
items.title_ko: 메타모델 연구 — TabPFN, 수십 GPU시간 걸리는 LLM 미세조정 메타모델을 수 초 만에 능가
items.summary: 이 논문은 다른 모델의 학습 행동을 예측하는 '메타모델'을 다룬다. 최종 성능 예측, 학습곡선 예측, 하이퍼파라미터 선택을 모두 동일한 학습 응답 함수에 대한 질의로 재해석한다. 실제 언어모델 학습 기록을 수치 데이터로 취급했을 때, 기성 테이블형 in-context 학습기인 **TabPFN**이 여러 설정에서 미세조정된 LLM 메타모델과 동등하거나 더 나은 성능을 보였다. TabPFN은 작업별 가중치 업데이트 없이 수 초 만에 적합·예측이 가능한 반면, 기존 LLM 미세조정은 수십~수백 GPU시간이 필요하다. 또한 TabPFN에 Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks(KAN)를 결합하면 일부 예측 과제에서 정확도가 더 향상되며, 535B 파라미터 규모의 공개 학습 실행인 Marin Hero Run에 대한 사전 등록 예측도 수행했다.
items.why_it_matters: 학습 전에 훈련 결과를 예측할 수 있다면 불필요한 GPU 비용을 크게 줄일 수 있어, 대규모 모델 학습을 계획하는 MLOps 실무자에게 직접적인 비용 절감 시사점을 준다.
items.whats_different: 기존 연구가 토큰화된 설정값에 **LLM을 미세조정**하는 방식(수십~수백 GPU시간 소요)을 택한 것과 달리, 이 논문은 메타모델링을 텍스트 과제가 아닌 별도의 수치 모달리티로 보고 TabPFN 같은 테이블형 학습기를 활용한다.

items.title: Are You Getting Your Money’s Worth From AI?
items.abstract: The following article was originally published on James Shore’s Successful Software blog and is being republished here with the author’s permission. Software development has emerged as the biggest beneficiary of AI automation. One CIO I talked to recently, with 170 people in his organization, measured a 2.1x increase in productivity from AI. That productivity came at a cost. His top users of AI each spent $21,000 on tokens per month. Another engineering leader spends six to eight thousand dollars per engineer per month. This is not a trivial amount of money. Eventually, it has to come from somewhere, and it will probably come from your personnel budget. Now we’re talking about real consequences for real people’s lives. But there are also real business consequences for not acting. If you’re going to make those choices—and somebody is going to—they need to be good ones. So you need to know more than the costs; you need to know the benefits too. Are you getting a good return on your investment in AI? Is there another way of using AI that would be better? How do you know what you’re getting? Anecdotal reports abound, but the reasoning behind those anecdotes are often, to put it politely, not ideal. Some claims are outright fiction. Given the stakes, that’s a problem. In this essay series, I’ll show you how to assess the impact of AI on software development in your organization. It’s in four parts plus an epilogue: Why, and what not to do (this essay) Measuring delivery speed Measuring and modeling unintended consequences Modeling and forecasting business outcomes Epilogue: Notes for your CFO Why you need to quantify impact Engineering leaders everywhere are feeling pressure to do more with AI. But which approach is best? There are a lot of people with strident opinions about what to do, but not a lot of consensus, and even less hard data. Even if there were hard data, it’s not one-size-fits-all. A solution that works best for an internal IT development shop isn’t necessarily the one that works best for a startup, and the approach that’s best for a new product isn’t necessarily the one that’s best for a crafty legacy system. Faster approaches aren’t necessarily better, either. If you get twice as much done per person, but spend so much money on tokens that you have to cut your staff in half, have you actually seen any ROI? You might actually be better off with a more modest speed boost if it keeps your costs down. You can’t make these trade-offs from a gut feeling alone. In a famous METR study , engineers thought AI made them 49% faster than it actually did. 1 You have to measure impact to know what you’re actually getting. Don’t neglect costs Costs are much easier to measure than impact, but they’re not without their own challenges. The biggest one is subsidies. In the fight to gain market share, big AI firms are offering substantial discounts. One engineering leader told me each team member was spending thousands of dollars in tokens at the cost of a $200 subscription. Anthropic and OpenAI are constantly offering discounts and other promotions. At some point, these subsidies will end, and prices will go up. Or will they? Open-weight models and local inference are exerting downward pressure on token costs. Dedicated inference chips could make tokens cheaper. Routers promise to direct your prompts to the cheapest model for the job. Models could require fewer tokens to accomplish the same task as they become more capable. All of these factors could actually cause prices to go down. When you calculate ROI, don’t assume today’s costs are the ones you should model. Whether you think prices will go up, down, or remain the same, make your assumptions explicit, and consider modeling both optimistic and pessimistic scenarios. One more wrinkle: Adopting AI isn’t a matter of flipping a switch. People will need time to learn how to apply it. As with any big shift, change management isn’t to be underestimated. items.title_ko: AI 코딩 생산성, 실제로 돈값 하나? — 월 2.1만 달러 토큰 비용 사례로 본 ROI 측정의 함정
items.summary: 한 CIO는 170명 조직에서 AI로 생산성이 **2.1배** 증가했다고 측정했지만, 상위 사용자는 토큰 비용으로 월 2만 1천 달러를 썼다. 다른 리더는 엔지니어 1인당 월 6~8천 달러를 지출한다고 밝혔다. 저자는 METR 연구를 인용해 엔지니어들이 AI로 **49% 더 빨라졌다고 체감했지만 실제로는 그렇지 않았다**는 점을 지적하며, 체감이 아닌 실측이 필요하다고 주장한다. 또한 현재의 AI 비용은 빅테크의 시장점유 경쟁에 따른 보조금 효과일 수 있어, 향후 가격이 오르거나 내릴 가능성을 모두 고려해 낙관·비관 시나리오를 함께 모델링해야 한다고 조언한다.
items.why_it_matters: AI 도입 비용이 결국 인건비 예산에서 나올 수 있는 상황에서, 막연한 효용 체감이 아니라 실제 ROI를 정량적으로 평가하는 방법론이 엔지니어링 리더에게 시급히 필요하다.
items.whats_different: 기존의 단편적 사례 보고나 주관적 체감 평가 대신, 전달 속도·부작용·비즈니스 성과를 단계적으로 측정하고 모델링하는 4부작 방법론을 제시한다는 점이 다르다.
